newsitem.title: JAPAN: Petrobras, Argentina to raise funds in yen - sources.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras, Argentina to raise funds in yen - sources.

text.p: Brazilian state oil giant Petrobras and Argentina are planning to raise funds in yen in the near term, underwriters said on Friday.
Petrobras is considering launching 15 billion yen worth of samurai bonds, with a duration of more than five years.
"Petrobras has already gathered market information from Japanese securities firms to study market conditions," an underwriting source said.
From the information compiled, Petrobras will decide the timing of the launch, but there is still a possibility that it may not go ahead if conditions are not appropriate.

Meanwhile, following the issuance of 50 billion yen worth of samurai bonds in December, Argentina is planning to launch another 50 billion yen, but this time in Euroyen bonds, as soon as next week, they said.
The duration of the Argentina issue is rumoured to be seven years and the coupon to be set around 4.2 percent, they said.
Underwriting sources said that Yamaichi Securities was appointed lead-manager for the Argentine issue.
Besides these, South Africa is expected to select a lead manager for its samurai bonds by the end of April.
Underwriters were unsure about the volume that South Africa would launch because the nation is also planning to issue U.S. dollar-based bonds around the same time.
South Africa's last issued samurai bonds in 1995 and the amount was about 30 billion yen, underwriters said.
